question.text: In relative valuation, Trading Multiples differ from Transaction Multiples in that:

answer.text: Trading multiples use listed market prices while transaction multiples use prices paid in M&A deals
They are exactly the same concept
Trading multiples use book values while transaction multiples use market values
Trading multiples are for bonds while transaction multiples are for equity

explanation.text: The Logic: Trading multiples are derived from prevailing stock market prices of listed comparable companies. Transaction multiples are derived from actual prices paid in similar consummated M&A transactions. Pages 212-213 of the NISM Series XV Research Analyst workbook (February 2026) draw this distinction directly. The Trap: The two are not the same, do not relate to book vs. market value, and are not split between bonds and equity. The only source-supported distinction is the price source: listed market prices vs. completed-transaction prices. Note: Claims about control premium, acquisition premium, or transaction multiples being typically higher than trading multiples are not found on pages 212-213 and are not relied on here.
